answer.rationale: Two candidate causes: the release (2h ago) or settlement-peak write load. The latency began climbing 90 minutes ago, which aligns temporally with the release rather than with a predictable daily traffic peak that provisioned headroom normally absorbs (b3 pattern). A regression in the release touching the write path is the strongest hypothesis, so I intend rollback_release. I verify b1 to confirm rollback safety/completion (its archived record says prior build was stable and rollback finished without customer impact) and b5 to keep route_read_replicas (offloading read pressure from the primary) as the fallback if verification shows rollback is unsafe (e.g., the new release changed write schemas). Execution is guarded (small_guarded_test) because settlement traffic is at peak: roll back in a controlled manner, watch write-path p99 and rollback health, and broaden only if the write path recovers as b1 predicts. Cause is not yet certain; rollback is reversible and diagnostic as well as therapeutic. Downstream value risk is flagged because losing customer writes is the stated constraint, and any rollback during settlement peak carries that theoretical exposure until b1's archived record is re-checked.
